subject: Sealed Root Key split policy + deployment gate for private (VPC/on-prem)
messages:

To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Sealed root key split policy + isolation questions for on‑prem stack

Hi Kimberly / Tessa,

Thanks again for the architecture review last week. We have a follow-up from our security and compliance committee: they want a short written policy that covers the sealed root key split for our private deployment (VPC + on‑prem HSMs) and a clear network "sequester" model that prevents any inadvertent key exfiltration during normal operation and rotation.

High level asks:
- A one-page canonical policy for how we split the root key material (operator roles, quorum, recovery steps).
- A recommended network gating design (what ports, which egress proxies, explicit jumpboxes) and where Redwood requires control-plane connectivity.
- Evidence items we can hand to our auditors (logs, attestation artifacts, rotation schedule template).

We attached our internal audit template and a brief list of questions — can you respond with the draft policy and a proposed gate timeline? Our compliance window is tight (ISO/SOC audit in mid‑March).

Files attached: meditech-audit-template.xlsx (referenced)

Appreciate the help,
Asha Patel
Director, Cloud Security
MediTech Health Systems
asha.patel@meditech.com
+1 415 555 0192

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@meditech.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Sealed root key split policy + isolation questions for on‑prem stack

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first draft of a sealed root key split policy (rootkey-split-policy-draft.pdf) and a short checklist for the audit handoff. Quick summary below and proposed next steps:

Summary (short):
- We recommend a 3-of-5 quorum for root key unseal split between Meditech custodians and two independent Redwood witnesses (no single party can unseal).
- Operators hold encrypted key shares stored in on‑prem HSMs; the root master remains sealed in the HSM and is never exported in clear.
- Recovery requires: two Meditech custodians + one Redwood witness, with manual verification steps logged (photo/ID + ticket reference) — details in the draft.

Network gating notes (high level):
- Control plane: required outbound to api.redwood-inference.com over TLS on port 443 from the management jumpbox only (explicit allow list).
- HSM connectivity: prefer private cross-connect or direct VCN/VPC peering; if using vendor-managed HSMs, require mutual TLS + certificate pinning to vendor endpoints.
- No direct HSM egress allowed from tenant subnets; only bastion/jump host permitted to initiate HSM sessions.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the attached draft and comment inline by Feb 17.
2) Schedule a 60‑minute call with our infra/HSM architect (Jonas) to walk the network diagram — I suggest Feb 20 or 21.
3) We will produce the evidence bundle (attestation artifacts, rotation timeline) within 5 business days after we align on the policy.

I've CC'd Jonas for technical detail and Marissa for compliance handoff.

Attachments: rootkey-split-policy-draft.pdf, audit-handoff-checklist.txt

—
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Integration
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Asha Patel <asha.patel@meditech.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 10:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Sealed root key split policy + isolation questions for on‑prem stack

Asha / team — following up with the technical sketch and constraints. See attached network-sequester-diagram.vsdx. Key design decisions:

- Physical/network separation: tenant compute and HSM management plane must be on separate subnets and different routing tables. HSM management traffic is only permitted from an auditable bastion in the management VPC via static ACLs.
- Egress minimization: only allow outbound to Redwood control plane from the bastion; block 0.0.0.0/0 from HSM management interfaces.
- HSM sessions: use mTLS + client certs stored in HSM (where supported) or use HSM-backed key wrapping tokens. No plaintext key material leaves the appliance.
- Time-limited session tokens: all unseal operations use short-lived tokens (TTL <= 15 minutes) and require a JIRA ticket reference and two custodian approvals before the token is issued.

Implementation caveats / questions for Meditech:
1) Do you have a preferred cross-connect provider (Equinix / AWS Direct Connect / GCP Interconnect)? This affects our recommended firewall ACL templates.
2) Can you confirm whether the HSM vendor supports remote attestation APIs (e.g., HSM firmware-signed quotes)? If not, we'll capture additional evidence via periodic on-site attestation.

I'll be available on Feb 20 to go through the diagram.

Attachments: network-sequester-diagram.vsdx

—Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@meditech.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 14:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Sealed root key split policy + isolation questions for on‑prem stack

Asha — adding the rollout/rotation checklist and auditor evidence template (see rotation-checklist.csv). A few operational items to align on:

- Rotation windows: quarterly key rotations for intermediate keys; sealed root key rekey (ceremony) limited to 18 months or on-significant infra change.
- Canary/rollback: we require a staged rollout (dev -> staging -> prod) with automated verification hooks. If any integrity check fails, the system must abort and require manual remediation.
- Audit artifacts: we will provide signed attestation bundles including: JVMTicket IDs, signed audit logs from the HSM, and PKI cert validation chains.

Request: please confirm custodians' names and contact details so we can pre-provision admin workflows and schedule the dry-run ceremony.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com

- Cross-connect: we will use Equinix colocation + AWS Direct Connect for the primary HSM link; ops-eng@bigcorp.com will handle the network procurement.
- HSM attestation: our vendor (CloudHSM Inc) supports firmware-signed attestation quotes — I've CC'd Luke Reynolds from CloudHSM to confirm the API endpoints and the expected evidence format.

Proposed schedule:

Attached: poc-request.docx (contains the procurement and POC checklist for CloudHSM Inc). I'll route the Equinix order this week.
